    Prospective Poisson surveillance threshold

    Source: R/surveillance-spatial.R
    epi_surveillance.Rd

    Uses a trailing window of preceding counts to estimate a constant Poisson mean and flags the current count if it exceeds the (1-alpha) Poisson quantile. This is a simple screening rule, not a validated outbreak detection system: it ignores seasonality, trends, reporting delays and changes in population. With family = "negbin", a negative binomial null is used whose dispersion is estimated by moments from the same window (Poisson when the window variance does not exceed its mean); short windows give unstable dispersion. Each screened row gets an upper-tail p-value, and adjust applies stats::p.adjust() across all screened rows. Flags are not outbreak diagnoses.

    Usage

    epi_surveillance(
  .data,
  cases,
  window = 4L,
  alpha = 0.05,
  family = c("poisson", "negbin"),
  adjust = "none"
)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame in chronological order at regular intervals.

    cases

    Non-negative integer counts.

    window

    Number of preceding observations in the baseline.

    alpha

    Nominal upper-tail probability, strictly between zero and one.

    family

    Null count model: "poisson" or "negbin".

    adjust

    Multiple-testing adjustment passed to stats::p.adjust().

    Value

    Input tibble with baseline mean, threshold, p-value, adjusted p-value and logical alert columns. These are NA for the first window rows.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(day = 1:6, cases = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 10))
epi_surveillance(d, cases, window = 3, alpha = 0.05)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>     day cases baseline_mean threshold     p_value  p_adjusted alert
#>   <int> <dbl>         <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1     1     1         NA           NA NA          NA          NA   
#> 2     2     2         NA           NA NA          NA          NA   
#> 3     3     1         NA           NA NA          NA          NA   
#> 4     4     2          1.33         3  0.385       0.385      FALSE
#> 5     5     1          1.67         4  0.811       0.811      FALSE
#> 6     6    10          1.33         3  0.00000147  0.00000147 TRUE
